sections.title: Level 2 Introduction to Input Output
sections.content: In Level 2, the machine does not perform simple sorting only. It performs shifting along with transformation. This means that a number or word may change its form while moving to its position. For example, while shifting a number forward, its digits may be added or it may be multiplied by 2.

sections.title: Concept of Dual-End Shifting
sections.content:
In Dual-End Shifting, the machine places two elements in their correct positions in every step. One element is fixed at the left end and another at the right end. Example: Input: 8 3 6 1 5
Step 1: 1 8 3 6 5
Step 2: 1 3 8 5 6
Step 3: 1 3 5 6 8
Here in every step, one smaller element moves to the left side and one larger element moves to the right side.

sections.title: Mathematical Transformation (Number Changes)
sections.content: Sometimes when a number moves to its position, its value is changed. Common transformations include: 1. Taking the sum of digits. 2. Multiplying the number by 2. 3. Reversing the number. Example: If 34 is shifted and the digit sum rule is applied, then 3 + 4 = 7.

sections.title: Word Transformation
sections.content: In some questions, words are not only arranged alphabetically but also modified according to certain rules. For example: 1. The word with the highest number of vowels may come first. 2. Sorting may be based on the last letter of the word. 3. Letters may shift to the next letter in the alphabet such as A → B or C → D.

sections.title: Vowel Count Sorting
sections.content:
In this type of question, words are arranged based on the number of vowels they contain. The vowels are A, E, I, O, U. Example: Input: Team Play Cat
Team has 2 vowels, Play has 1 vowel, Cat has 1 vowel. Therefore Team comes first.

sections.title: Last Letter Sorting
sections.content:
Sometimes words are arranged according to their last letter. Example: Input: Mango Ball Cat
Last letters are: o, l, t
In alphabetical order it becomes l, o, t. Therefore the order will be Ball, Mango, Cat.

sections.title: Identifying Step Patterns
sections.content: In Level 2, carefully observe Input, Step 1, Step 2, and Step 3. Identify which two elements are getting fixed and check whether any transformation is happening. Usually, two elements reach their final position in every step.

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content: 1. Not recognizing dual-end shifting. 2. Ignoring the transformation rule. 3. Making mistakes while counting vowels. 4. Not understanding alphabetical order together with transformation rules.

sections.title: Quick Summary
sections.content: Level 2 Input Output mainly includes two concepts: shifting and transformation. In each step, two elements may get fixed and sometimes their values or letters may also change. Analyzing the initial steps carefully is necessary to identify the pattern.

tricks.title: Identify Dual-End Pattern
tricks.explanation: If in Step 1 one element is fixed at the extreme left and another at the extreme right, then it is dual-end shifting.

tricks.title: Check Transformation Immediately
tricks.explanation: If the shifted number looks different from the original number, a transformation rule is applied.

tricks.title: Digit Sum Identification Trick
tricks.explanation: If a large number suddenly becomes smaller, often the digit sum rule is used.

tricks.title: Multiply Pattern Recognition
tricks.explanation: If a number suddenly becomes double, the rule might be multiplication by 2.

tricks.title: Vowel Counting Trick
tricks.explanation: First write the number of vowels for each word and then perform sorting.

tricks.title: Last Letter Order Trick
tricks.explanation: Write the last letters of the words separately and arrange them alphabetically.

tricks.title: Alphabet Next Letter Rule
tricks.explanation: If words change, each letter may shift to the next letter in the alphabet.

tricks.title: Step Count Identification
tricks.explanation: In dual-end shifting, final output usually appears in about n/2 steps.

tricks.title: Step Comparison Method
tricks.explanation: Compare Input with Step 1, and Step 1 with Step 2 to identify the pattern quickly.

tricks.title: Final Output Estimation
tricks.explanation: Once the sorting rule is clear, mentally sort the entire sequence to quickly find the final output.
